title: Sunday Collars
subject: a woman teaching her new boyfriend to iron his own work shirts on a Sunday night: steam hissing, collars first, and the one blue shirt he scorches, which she keeps as a nightshirt
caption: New jack swing revival, late-80s Teddy Riley swing groove with 2020s polish. Swung drum-machine beat with a big gated snare and shuffling hi-hats; a bouncing synth bass; bright DX-style electric piano stabs on the offbeats; slap bass fills and finger snaps between lines. Glossy late-80s mix with modern low end, close lead vocal. Male tenor, smooth R&B lead with stacked falsetto harmonies on the hook. 104 BPM, Bb major. Tender, teasing and quietly smitten. No trap drums, no autotune, no modern pop drop, no rock guitar solo, no ballad tempo.
lyrics:
[Intro - gated snare, electric piano stabs, snaps]

[Verse 1]
Sunday night, the board squeaks open wide
Five white shirts are piled up by my side
You fill the iron, tap it twice
Say collars first, I'll say it nice

[Pre-Chorus]
Steam goes hiss across the room
You hum along to the tune

[Chorus]
Collar, cuffs, then the sleeves
Your hand on mine, I don't want to leave
Collar, cuffs, then the back
Keep teaching me slow like that

[Verse 2]
Phone goes off, I turn to look
Smoke comes up like a burning book
My one blue shirt, a brown iron mark
You laugh and say, well, that's your mark

[Chorus]
Collar, cuffs, then the sleeves
You grab the blue one, say it's yours to keep
Collar, cuffs, then the back
You wear it now, I want it back

[Bridge - bass and snaps only]
Monday morning, collar crisp and new
Still smells like Sunday, steam and you

[Outro - stacked falsetto, piano stabs fade]
Collar, cuffs, collar, cuffs
Sunday nights with you are enough
